doc_verification.detail: Reachability PASS: page + .md variant both fetched via alternate web reader on 2026-09-04 (native WebFetch domain-verifier blocked api.qdrant.tech; recorded honestly). Version PASS: page selector shows v1.18.x (URL path v-1-18-x), matching target v1.18.0 on major.minor. Content PARTIAL: the page documents POST /collections/{collection_name}/points/delete with a 'PointIdsList OR FilterSelector' body and a 200 UpdateResult response, but the rendered response section carries ONLY the 200 branch — the literal promise '400 on an invalid filter' is not verbatim prose on the fetched page; it is grounded in (a) the contract's own embedded doc-verification record (doc_quote '...200 ok, 404 for a missing collection, 400 for an invalid filter', verified_at 2026-09-02T12:34:08Z) and (b) the server's own demonstrated convention (T1/m1/m4/F3/F4 all returned 400 'Format error in JSON body' for shape-invalid filters). Note also the Fern-rendered schema for must/must_not/should explicitly lists single-object alternatives ('object or ... or list of object ... or any'), so the OBJECT CONTAINER itself is doc-schema-legal; the violation rests on the no-matcher condition, which the source's own validator defines as invalid. Endpoint precision PASS: endpoint_registry maps points+delete to POST /collections/{collection_name}/points/delete with the same source_url; the script used exactly this path.

http_semantics.note: Worse than a business error code: the request-decidable invalid filter (no-matcher condition) returned HTTP 200 with a full SUCCESS envelope (status:"ok", operation_id:3, status:"completed") — the invalidity was not surfaced as an error anywhere in the response, and the operation executed destructively.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok (UpdateResult) on success; 404 when the collection is missing; 400 on an invalid filter
contract_grounding.note: assertion_text_quoted is the verbatim description field of qdrant_behavioral_points_delete_001 in structured_contract.json (~line 7153); the same entry's expected_behavior field additionally reads verbatim: 'valid delete returns HTTP 200; missing collection returns 404; malformed filter returns 400'. violates-declaration self-check: the observed phenomenon is 'invalid filter silently accepted with 200 + destructive execution', and the quoted constraint demands '400 on an invalid filter' — the observed input IS inside the constraint's invalid-filter domain. Ground for 'invalid': the source's own validator explicitly defines a FieldCondition with no matcher as invalid (types.rs:3232-3240 'At least one field condition must be specified'), and the server's own convention returns 400 for shape-invalid filters on sibling faces (T1, m1, m4, F3, F4 all 400 'Format error in JSON body'). Caveat recorded for the auditor: the object-instead-of-array CONTAINER is by-design one-or-many (MaybeOneOrMany) and doc-schema-legal; the violating substance is the no-matcher condition acceptance (and its destructive must_not inversion), not the container shape.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: Request {"filter":{"must_not":{"key":"grp"}}} -> actix delete_points (src/actix/api/update_api.rs:80, Json<PointsSelector>, serde-untagged) -> FilterSelector -> Filter.must_not via MaybeOneOrMany map-branch -> vec![Condition] (lib/segment/src/common/utils.rs:104) -> Condition::deserialize routes map-with-'key' to FieldCondition (types.rs:3442-3449) -> FieldCondition{key:"grp", all matchers None} (types.rs:3040-3067, every matcher Option => serde-legal). The VALIDATION that would reject this exists in source — PointsSelector:Validate (lib/collection/src/operations/point_ops.rs:28-35) cascades Filter#[validate(nested)] -> FieldCondition#[validate(schema(function="validate_field_condition"))] -> 'At least one field condition must be specified' (types.rs:3232-3240), and unit tests assert batch.validate().is_err() for invalid selectors (point_ops.rs:403-427) — but NO .validate() call exists anywhere on the REST path (handler -> do_delete_points src/common/update.rs:412 -> update() :1201 -> TableOfContent::update lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/point_ops.rs:490; grep of src/ + lib/collection + lib/storage update chain finds zero call sites). Evaluation then proceeds: no payload index on 'grp' -> fallback field_condition.check per value (query_checker.rs:234) -> check_match with all-None matchers returns false for every point (condition_checker.rs:78-101) -> check_must_not inverts (!false=true) for every point (query_checker.rs:88-97) -> filter matches ALL 6 remaining points -> DeletePointsByFilter wipes them -> observed count 6->0. Root cause: no-matcher FieldCondition passes serde and the validator that forbids it is never invoked on the REST delete path.
source_grounding.outcome_note: validation_absent on the operative path, with precision: the validation RULE exists in source (validator-crate impls at every level, tested in lib/collection/src/operations/point_ops.rs:403-427) but is never invoked on the REST delete-points route — dead validation code, so the API accepts an input the source itself defines as invalid, with destructive effect. NOT by_design_in_source: the only by-design element is the one-or-many object shorthand (MaybeOneOrMany, unit-tested, mirrored by the Fern doc schema 'object or ... or list of object'); nothing annotates acceptance of matcher-less conditions — the source's own validator text points the opposite way. Corroboration that this generalizes beyond the shorthand: state_points_delete_002 m3 shows a well-formed ARRAY containing a no-matcher condition also accepted 200 on the same endpoint.

mundane_explanation.surviving: By-design defense is available ONLY for the one-object shorthand container (MaybeOneOrMany, unit-tested, doc-schema-visible); it does NOT cover acceptance of a matcher-less FieldCondition, which the source's own validator explicitly forbids ('At least one field condition must be specified') yet is never enforced on the REST path. The surviving defect signal: an explicitly-forbidden filter shape is silently accepted AND destructively executed (must_not:[no-matcher condition] inverts to match-everything, wiping the collection) — the destructive generalization of the gap is confirmed by the same-endpoint m3 (array form) and m2 (null clause -> empty filter -> wipe) observations.
